insights.concise_text: PitchNet addresses BIBREF0's difficulty on learning joint representation of phonetic and pitch representation by adding an adversarially trained pitch regression network and extracted pitch input to the decoder.

triple.subject: PitchNet
triple.object: difficulty on learning joint representation of phonetic and pitch representation

insights.concise_text: The pitch regression loss makes the whole model obtain pitch information from $p(s^j)$, which is the extracted pitch fed into the decoder after linear interpolation.

triple.subject: pitch regression loss
triple.object: extracted pitch $p(s^j)$ as decoder input

insights.concise_text: PitchNet's claim of greatly improving converted voice quality is supported by Mean Opinion Score (MOS) results where naturalness and similarity are both higher than the other two ones.

triple.subject: Mean Opinion Score (MOS) results
triple.object: PitchNet's greatly improved converted voice quality

insights.concise_text: PitchNet's flexible pitch manipulation is evidenced by multiplying input pitch by 0.7, 1.0 and 1.3 and observing output pitch changes significantly along with input pitch.

triple.subject: input pitch multiplied by 0.7, 1.0 and 1.3
triple.object: output pitch changes significantly along with input pitch

insights.concise_text: The pitch regression network that separates pitch information out of the latent space is trained adversarially using $\mathcal {L}_{ad}$ while the whole model uses $\mathcal {L}_{total}$.

triple.subject: pitch regression network
triple.object: alternate optimization with $\mathcal {L}_{ad}$ and $\mathcal {L}_{total}$

insights.concise_text: The singer classification loss(also named domain confusion loss BIBREF0) corresponds to the confusion loss BIBREF12 used in BIBREF0 to force a singer-invariant representation.

triple.subject: singer classification loss(also named domain confusion loss BIBREF0)
triple.object: confusion loss BIBREF12

insights.concise_text: PitchNet was evaluated on the male part of NUS-48E BIBREF14 dataset, where each one's singing voice was converted to the other five singer's voice.

triple.subject: PitchNet
triple.object: male part of NUS-48E BIBREF14 dataset

insights.concise_text: The automatic score using normalized cross correlation (NCC) showed PitchNet performed better than USVC (our) on conversion and reconstruction tasks.

triple.subject: PitchNet
triple.object: USVC (our) on conversion and reconstruction tasks

insights.concise_text: Because only reconstruction loss is not enough to learn conversion, PitchNet adds singer classification loss and pitch regression loss adversarially to the reconstruction loss.

triple.subject: only reconstruction loss insufficiency
triple.object: adversarial singer classification loss and pitch regression loss addition

insights.concise_text: The conclusion that PitchNet outperforms the existing unsupervised singing voice conversion method is supported by comparisons against USVC(our) using automatic evaluation score and human evaluation score.

triple.subject: automatic evaluation score and human evaluation score comparisons against USVC(our)
triple.object: PitchNet outperforms the existing unsupervised singing voice conversion method
